text:
Kevin Stenlund is a defensive centre, a Stanley Cup winner with Florida in 2024, and Utah uses him that way, about 13 and a half minutes a night in a checking role. He has five points in 21 games and none in his last eleven.

Unlike some droughts on this team, this one isn't bad luck. We'd have expected about 3.1 points over those eleven games, and the looks have thinned out. His own shots are worth 0.36 expected goals per 60, lower than last season, and Utah takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, almost 6 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 1% of forwards for creating offense last season, so none of this is new.

The point of him is elsewhere, in the defensive matchups, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says as much: his value, if it's there, doesn't show at five on five. Our model compares him to Oskar Sundqvist and Jordan Greenway. With Utah's lineup patched together, the question is whether the Mammoth can afford a fourth-line centre who doesn't drive play. Our talent range has him around 7 goals.
